newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: EU to seek WTO panel on Indonesian car policy.
newsitem.headline: EU to seek WTO panel on Indonesian car policy.

text.p: The European Union will next week ask fellow members of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) to agree to set up a panel to look into Indonesia's controversial national car policy, trade diplomats said on Tuesday.
The move follows a similar request by Japan which was blocked by Indonesia at the last meeting of the WTO's Dispute Settlement Body (DSB) on April 30.

The United States has also been in consultations with Indonesia over the policy, which offers 100 percent exemptions from tariffs and taxes to national automakers, and is widely expected to seek a panel itself.

All three powers argue that the concessions, which so far have benefited only a joint venture between a company headed by a son of Indonesian President Suharto and South Korea's Kia Motors Corp., discriminate against their own automobiles.
Jakarta has rejected their complaints, insisting it is not violating WTO rules.

And last week a top official of the Indonesian company, Timor Putra Nasional which produces a sedan known as the Timor at a Kia plant in South Korea, said it would also start importing a small sports car from there early next year.
Trade envoys in Geneva said the announcement had angered many governments. "It looks as though the Indonesians plan to fight this case right down the line," said one.
But Japanese officials said they would not be pressing for a panel at the next DSB meeting on May 23. "This will give the Indonesians more time to reconsider what they are doing," one commented.
Had Tokyo persisted, a panel would have been set up automatically under WTO rules, which only allow members to block a request once.
